title: MERN Stack Assessment
description: Comprehensive test on MongoDB, Express.js, React, Node.js, RESTful architecture, and state management.

questions.questionText: Which MongoDB aggregation pipeline stage is used to filter documents in a collection?
options: $group
$project
$match
$filter
questions.explanation: $match filters the documents to pass only the documents that match the specified condition(s) to the next pipeline stage.

questions.questionText: In Express.js, what does the next() function do inside custom middleware?
options: Terminates the current HTTP request
Passes control to the next middleware or route handler in the stack
Restarts the Express application
Redirects the client to another URL
questions.explanation: Calling next() hands off execution to the subsequent middleware function in the chain.

questions.questionText: In React, what is the purpose of the cleanup function returned inside useEffect?
options: To clear browser LocalStorage
To reset component state to initial values
To clean up subscriptions, timers, or event listeners before the component unmounts or before re-running the effect
To trigger an immediate re-render
questions.explanation: The return function in useEffect cleans up side-effects like subscriptions, timers, or abort controllers before re-executing or unmounting.

questions.questionText: Which Node.js core module is primarily responsible for handling file system operations?
options: path
fs
http
events
questions.explanation: The 'fs' module provides an API for interacting with the file system (both synchronous and asynchronous/promises).

questions.questionText: What is the primary difference between SQL databases and MongoDB?
options: SQL is NoSQL and MongoDB is relational
SQL uses tables with rigid schemas; MongoDB is document-oriented with flexible JSON-like BSON schemas
MongoDB does not support indexes
SQL databases cannot store numbers
questions.explanation: MongoDB stores records as dynamic BSON documents without rigid schema constraints, unlike relational tabular SQL databases.

questions.questionText: In React, why must hooks never be called inside conditional statements or loops?
options: They will throw a syntax error during compilation
React relies on the call order of hooks remaining identical between renders to preserve state
Conditional statements cause memory leaks in JavaScript
Hooks can only be called in plain JavaScript files
questions.explanation: React maintains hook state by tracking the exact index/order in which hooks are invoked on each render.

questions.questionText: What HTTP status code should be returned when a resource is successfully created via a POST request?
options: 200 OK
201 Created
204 No Content
302 Found
questions.explanation: HTTP 201 Created indicates that the request has succeeded and led to the creation of a new resource.

questions.questionText: What is the role of Mongoose pre-save middleware in a MERN application?
options: To validate incoming HTTP request cookies
To execute custom logic (such as hashing passwords) before document persistence
To send automated emails to clients
To bundle frontend React assets
questions.explanation: pre('save') hooks allow developers to intercept the document lifecycle immediately before writing to MongoDB.

questions.questionText: What is the Virtual DOM in React and why is it beneficial?
options: A direct copy of the browser DOM stored in Web Workers
An in-memory lightweight representation of the actual DOM used to compute efficient batched updates via reconciliation
A plugin that connects React with MongoDB
A browser extension for debugging React components
questions.explanation: React diffs the in-memory Virtual DOM against previous snapshots to calculate minimal real DOM updates.

questions.questionText: What does CORS stand for in web development and why is it enforced?
options: Cross-Origin Resource Sharing; enforced by browsers to prevent unauthorized cross-origin requests
Central Operating Routing System; enforced by Node.js to manage ports
Client Online Registration Standard; enforced by MongoDB for access control
Cascading Object Reference Sheets; used for CSS styling
questions.explanation: CORS is a browser security mechanism that restricts web applications from requesting resources on different origins without explicit server permission.

title: Web Dev Fundamentals
description: Essential web development concepts including HTML5 semantic tags, CSS Box Model, Flexbox/Grid, and HTTP.

questions.questionText: Which HTML5 semantic element is most suitable for standalone, syndicated content such as a blog post or news story?
options: <div>
<section>
<article>
<aside>
questions.explanation: <article> represents a self-contained composition that is independently distributable or reusable.

questions.questionText: In CSS layout, which property changes the box sizing so that padding and border are included in an element's total width and height?
options: box-sizing: content-box
box-sizing: border-box
display: flex
margin: auto
questions.explanation: border-box includes padding and borders in the element's total declared width and height.

questions.questionText: Which HTTP header is utilized by the client to send a Bearer authentication token?
options: Content-Type
Authorization
Accept
X-Auth-Token
questions.explanation: The standard 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' header conveys credentials to authenticate requests.

questions.questionText: In CSS Flexbox, which property controls alignment along the cross-axis?
options: justify-content
align-items
flex-direction
flex-wrap
questions.explanation: align-items aligns items along the cross-axis, whereas justify-content aligns along the main axis.

questions.questionText: What is the primary difference between localStorage and sessionStorage?
options: localStorage only stores numbers, sessionStorage stores strings
localStorage persists until explicitly cleared, while sessionStorage expires when the page session / browser tab closes
sessionStorage has an unlimited storage quota
localStorage is sent with every HTTP request automatically
questions.explanation: localStorage data has no expiration date; sessionStorage is scoped to the current browser tab session.

questions.questionText: Which HTTP method is considered idempotent?
options: POST
PUT
PATCH (without precondition)
CONNECT
questions.explanation: PUT is idempotent: making multiple identical requests has the same effect as making a single request.

questions.questionText: What does CSS specificity decide when multiple CSS rules match the same element?
options: The file size of the CSS stylesheet
Which style declaration takes precedence based on selector weight (inline > IDs > classes > elements)
The loading order of images
How fast JavaScript executes
questions.explanation: Specificity is the weight algorithm browsers use to resolve conflicting CSS declarations.

questions.questionText: Which meta tag is crucial for responsive mobile rendering?
options: <meta charset='UTF-8'>
<meta name='viewport' content='width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0'>
<meta http-equiv='X-UA-Compatible' content='IE=edge'>
<meta name='robots' content='index, follow'>
questions.explanation: The viewport meta tag instructs the browser how to control the page's dimensions and scaling on mobile screens.

title: JavaScript Core & Async Mastery
description: Deep-dive into closures, prototypes, event loops, promises, async/await, and modern ECMAScript features.

questions.questionText: What is a closure in JavaScript?
options: A method that terminates an open database connection
A function bundled with references to its surrounding lexical environment
An IIFE that clears the call stack
A tool for minifying code
questions.explanation: A closure gives an inner function access to its outer scope even after the outer function has finished executing.

questions.questionText: What is the output of typeof null in JavaScript?
options: 'null'
'undefined'
'object'
'boolean'
questions.explanation: typeof null returns 'object' due to a historical legacy bug in the initial JavaScript implementation.

questions.questionText: Which queue has higher priority in the JavaScript Event Loop?
options: Macrotask queue (e.g. setTimeout, setInterval)
Microtask queue (e.g. Promise callbacks, queueMicrotask)
I/O polling queue
They have equal round-robin priority
questions.explanation: The microtask queue is processed completely after the current execution context and before the next macrotask.

questions.questionText: What does Promise.all() do when one of the passed promises rejects?
options: It ignores the rejected promise and returns the resolved ones
It immediately rejects with the reason of the first rejected promise (fail-fast)
It waits for all promises and returns null
It throws an uncatchable syntax error
questions.explanation: Promise.all() rejects immediately upon any rejection. For waiting on all results regardless of outcome, Promise.allSettled() is used.

questions.questionText: What is the difference between == and === in JavaScript?
options: == compares value with type coercion; === performs strict equality without coercion
=== only compares numbers
== is faster than ===
There is no difference
questions.explanation: Strict equality (===) checks both value and type, whereas loose equality (==) coerces types before comparison.

questions.questionText: What is variable hoisting in JavaScript?
options: Uploading variables to a cloud server
The process where variable and function declarations are moved to the top of their containing scope during compilation
Deleting unused variables to free RAM
Converting local variables into global variables
questions.explanation: Declarations are evaluated before any code is executed; var is initialized with undefined, while let/const remain in Temporal Dead Zone (TDZ).

questions.questionText: Which method creates a new array populated with the results of calling a provided function on every element in the calling array?
options: filter()
forEach()
map()
reduce()
questions.explanation: Array.prototype.map() returns a brand new array with transformed elements without mutating the original array.

questions.questionText: What is the effect of using 'use strict' in a JavaScript file?
options: Prevents execution on older browsers
Catches silent errors, disallows global variable creation without declaration, and prohibits obsolete features
Enforces TypeScript static types at runtime
Compresses the JavaScript code automatically
questions.explanation: Strict mode enforces stricter parsing and error handling, turning silent bugs into throwing exceptions.

title: Node.js & Express API Security
description: Essential backend security practices including JWT, bcrypt, rate limiting, sanitization, and CORS.

questions.questionText: Why should passwords never be hashed with plain MD5 or SHA-256 for user authentication?
options: They take too much RAM to compute
They are fast non-salted cryptographic algorithms vulnerable to rainbow tables and high-speed GPU brute force
They cannot hash strings longer than 10 characters
Node.js does not support them
questions.explanation: Modern password hashing requires slow, adaptive algorithms like bcrypt or Argon2 with built-in salts to resist brute force.

questions.questionText: What is the primary vulnerability prevented by helmet middleware in Express?
options: Database connection drops
Common web vulnerabilities (XSS, clickjacking, MIME-sniffing) by configuring secure HTTP response headers
Syntax errors in JavaScript
Slow network connections
questions.explanation: Helmet sets HTTP headers such as Content-Security-Policy, X-Frame-Options, and Strict-Transport-Security.

questions.questionText: What is a SQL / NoSQL Injection attack and how is it prevented in Mongoose?
options: Injecting CSS styles into database tables
Malicious queries passed via client input; prevented in Mongoose via schema validation and sanitized parameterized queries
Crashing the server by uploading large files
Stealing tokens from localStorage
questions.explanation: Injection occurs when untrusted input is executed as database query logic. Input validation and parameterized query models prevent it.

questions.questionText: What is the difference between Authentication and Authorization?
options: Authentication verifies WHO you are; Authorization determines WHAT you are allowed to do
Authentication is on the frontend; Authorization is on the backend
Authentication uses passwords; Authorization only uses facial recognition
They are synonymous terms
questions.explanation: Authentication checks identity (e.g. login). Authorization checks permissions (e.g. Admin role access).

questions.questionText: Where should sensitive configuration keys (like JWT_SECRET and Database Passwords) be stored in production?
options: Hardcoded directly into GitHub repository files
In secured environment variables / secrets managers, excluded from source control via .gitignore
In the browser's localStorage
In public HTML meta tags
questions.explanation: Secrets must never be checked into version control and must be injected via environment variables at runtime.

questions.questionText: What is the purpose of API Rate Limiting (e.g., express-rate-limit)?
options: To speed up the internet connection for all users
To protect endpoints against brute force, credential stuffing, and Denial of Service (DoS) attacks
To limit how many database tables can be created
To limit the length of URLs
questions.explanation: Rate limiting caps the number of requests an IP can make within a specified time window.

title: React Performance & Architecture
description: Master React optimization techniques: useMemo, useCallback, code splitting, memoization, and custom hooks.

questions.questionText: When should React.memo be used on a component?
options: On every single component in an application by default
When a component re-renders frequently with the exact same props and involves expensive rendering logic
Only on components that do not have state
Only in Next.js applications
questions.explanation: React.memo skips re-rendering when props haven't changed, preventing wasteful render cycles on costly components.

questions.questionText: What does useCallback do in React?
options: Caches the return value of a calculated function
Returns a memoized version of the callback function that only changes if dependencies change
Calls an external API asynchronously
Forces a component to re-mount
questions.explanation: useCallback preserves function reference equality across renders, preventing unwanted child re-renders.

questions.questionText: What is React code splitting and how is it commonly achieved?
options: Splitting JavaScript into multiple files using React.lazy() and dynamic import() to reduce initial bundle size
Dividing one React component into multiple functions in the same file
Separating HTML from CSS styles
Splitting a database into multiple collections
questions.explanation: React.lazy() paired with Suspense enables lazy loading of route bundles on demand.

questions.questionText: Why should array indices generally be avoided as keys in dynamic React lists?
options: React will throw an error and refuse to render
Reordering, inserting, or deleting items can cause incorrect component state and inefficient DOM updates
Keys must always be integers
Array indices take up too much memory
questions.explanation: Using indices confuses React's reconciliation diffing when list items are sorted, deleted, or inserted.

questions.questionText: What is the primary advantage of custom React hooks?
options: They make the application run in Node.js instead of the browser
They extract and share stateful logic across multiple components without altering component hierarchy
They eliminate the need to use CSS
They automatically connect React to MongoDB
questions.explanation: Custom hooks allow modular reuse of stateful logic (like data fetching, authentication, or media queries).

title: Git & Collaborative Engineering
description: Essential version control skills: branching strategies, merge conflicts, pull requests, and CI/CD basics.

questions.questionText: What is the purpose of a .gitignore file?
options: To delete ignored files permanently from the hard drive
To instruct Git which untracked files and folders (e.g., node_modules, .env) should not be committed to version control
To ignore errors during code execution
To speed up internet upload speeds
questions.explanation: .gitignore specifies deliberately untracked files that Git should ignore when staging commits.

questions.questionText: What command creates and switches to a new branch in Git?
options: git branch <name>
git checkout -b <name>
git merge <name>
git pull -b <name>
questions.explanation: git checkout -b <name> (or git switch -c <name>) creates a new branch and checks it out immediately.

questions.questionText: What happens during a Git merge conflict?
options: The repository is corrupted and must be re-cloned
Two branches have contradictory changes to the same line in a file, requiring manual resolution
Git deletes both versions of the conflicting file
The server rejects all future commits
questions.explanation: A merge conflict occurs when automated merging cannot reconcile conflicting edits on the same lines.

questions.questionText: What is the primary benefit of Continuous Integration (CI)?
options: Writing code without needing developers
Automatically building, linting, and testing code changes on every commit or pull request to detect bugs early
Encrypting user passwords in the database
Hosting websites for free
questions.explanation: CI pipelines automate verification (linting, tests, builds) to maintain code quality before merging to main.
